```rca
{"headline": "Bugaboo's -15.7% YoY fall is a brand-specific volume loss (fewer units at an unchanged price) while the pram market grew; it is spread widely, with WA, QLD and TAS hit hardest.",

 "key_evidence": [{"label": "Bugaboo revenue YoY (28d to 7 May)", "value": "-15.7%"}, {"label": "Market (other P&S brands) YoY", "value": "+2.3%"}, {"label": "Share change vs LY", "value": "-4.2 pts"}, {"label": "Volume share of the revenue change", "value": "100.6%"}, {"label": "WA revenue YoY (36.7% of the fall)", "value": "-35%"}],
 "hypotheses": [{"hypothesis": "Whole market declining", "verdict": "RULED_OUT", "evidence": "Market +2.3% vs Bugaboo -15.7%; AUD -510K is brand-specific"},
  {"hypothesis": "Price/ASP drove the fall", "verdict": "RULED_OUT", "evidence": "ASP +0.1%; volume effect AUD -447K = 100.6% of change"},
  {"hypothesis": "Volume loss", "verdict": "CONFIRMED", "evidence": "Units 1,710 vs 2,031 (-15.8%)"},
  {"hypothesis": "One week or a sudden break", "verdict": "RULED_OUT", "evidence": "Last 4 wks -13.8% vs prior 12 wks -4.8%; under the 10-pt step rule"},
  {"hypothesis": "One state", "verdict": "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence": "WA -35% carries 36.7%; QLD -20.5% carries 29.7%; VIC +6.4%"},
  {"hypothesis": "One class", "verdict": "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence": "Capsule -22.2% carries 36.2%; Single Stroller +2.7%"},
  {"hypothesis": "One store", "verdict": "RULED_OUT", "evidence": "Biggest store (Mandurah) carries only 15.1% across 60 stores"},
  {"hypothesis": "Supply/stock-outs", "verdict": "RULED_OUT", "evidence": "DIFOT 88.8% vs 87.4% prior; OOS 1.9% vs market 1.8%"},
  {"hypothesis": "Competitor price gap", "verdict": "INCONCLUSIVE", "evidence": "No competitor price data in both years"}],
 "ruled_out": ["Market decline - the market grew 2.3%", "Price - ASP moved only +0.1%", "Supply - DIFOT improved and stock-outs match the market", "Single store or one-off week - spread across 60 stores, no spike or break"],
 "impact": "AUD -445K (-15.7%) vs LY and AUD -162K (-6.4%) vs the prior 28 days; share 34.3% to 30.1%. Week of 27 Apr was -26.7%, so the fall may be getting worse.",
 "actions": [{"owner": "Category", "action": "Look into WA, QLD and TAS range and display, and the worst stores (Mandurah -71.9%, Tea Tree Plaza -65.3%), against VIC's +6.4%"},
  {"owner": "Buying", "action": "Check the falling Capsule, Double and Accessory SKUs (e.g. Capsule Stroller 12 -60.7%) for range changes or launches that have aged"},
  {"owner": "Data", "action": "Load competitor price data for Bugaboo so we can test whether Uppababy or Silver Cross are taking share on price"},
  {"owner": "Marketing", "action": "Win back First-time Parent, Gift and Grandparent shoppers (-20% to -27%)"}],
 "learning": "Track Bugaboo's share every week, not just its revenue: the brand fell while its market grew, and the latest week's -26.7% points to a widening gap."}
```

## What is happening
Bugaboo made AUD 2.39M in the 28 days to 7 May 2026. That is down 15.7% (AUD -445K) on the same days last year and down 6.4% on the prior 28 days. The rest of the Prams & Strollers market grew 2.3% over the same period, so Bugaboo's share fell from 34.3% to 30.1%.

The whole fall comes from selling fewer units: 1,710 against 2,031 last year (-15.8%). The average selling price is flat (+0.1%) and margin slipped only 0.8 points, to 36.8%.

The fall is spread widely:
- **States:** WA is down 35%, QLD 20.5% and TAS 43.4%. VIC is the only state growing (+6.4%).
- **Classes:** Capsule Strollers are down 22.2% and Accessories 24.3%. Only Single Strollers are up (+2.7%).

The fall has deepened over time. Weekly sales ran about 5% below last year early in the year, then fell to -26.7% in the week of 27 April.



## What we tested
| Hypothesis | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Market decline | Market +2.3% vs Bugaboo -15.7%; AUD -510K of the fall is Bugaboo's own | Ruled out |
| Price vs volume | Units explain 100.6% of the change; price changed +0.1% | Volume confirmed |
| Sudden break in one week | Last 4 weeks -13.8% vs -4.8% before; below the 10-point threshold | Ruled out |
| One state | WA has 36.7% of the fall, QLD 29.7%; no single state has half | Inconclusive |
| One class | Capsule Strollers have 36.2% of the fall | Inconclusive |
| One store | The biggest contributor (Mandurah) has only 15.1% of the fall | Ruled out |
| Supply | Delivery rate (DIFOT) 88.8% vs 87.4% before; stock-outs 1.9% vs 1.8% for the market | Ruled out |
| Competitor price | No price data for both years | Inconclusive |

Confidence is Medium. Price, supply and a market-wide fall are ruled out, but no single state, class or store explains the decline. The likeliest unmeasured cause is competitors taking share, since we can't test their prices.

## What to do
- **Category:** Look into WA, QLD and TAS and the worst-hit stores, and compare them with VIC, which is growing.
- **Buying:** Review the falling Capsule, Double Stroller and Accessory products.
- **Data:** Load competitor price data, so we can check whether Uppababy or Silver Cross are winning on price.
- **Marketing:** Target First-time Parents, Gift Buyers and Grandparents, the customer groups falling fastest (-20% to -27%).
